sections.heading: The Andhra Mahasabha — a province imagined annually

blocks.text: The **Andhra Movement** demanded a Telugu-speaking province out of the composite Madras Presidency — grievances: Tamil-dominant administration, under-representation in services and legislature, neglect of Telugu districts' irrigation-education, and identity ('Andhrulu' as a historic people — the Satavahana-Kakatiya-Vijayanagara memory the renaissance had revived). Trigger-consciousness: the 1911-13 ferment (Bapatla-area conferences; the sting of being 'northern districts' of a Madras world). The **first Andhra Mahasabha met at Bapatla, 26-27 May 1913** (president **B.N. Sarma**; ~800 delegates) — resolving for a separate Andhra province; sessions thereafter annually carried the demand into Congress politics.

rows: **Bapatla 1913**
First Andhra Mahasabha; the founding resolution; the movement's Magna Carta
**Linguistic PCC victory (1917-18)**
Congress conceded a separate **Andhra Provincial Congress Committee** — Nagpur (1920) generalised linguistic PCCs: the Andhra demand reshaped Congress's own map
Inter-war pressure

Mahasabha sessions + Andhra University (1926) + **Sri Bagh Pact (1937)** — the internal settlement between Circars & **Rayalaseema** (guarantees on university, HC location, irrigation priority for Rayalaseema — the name 'Rayalaseema' itself coined by **Chilukuri Narayana Rao (1928)** replacing 'Ceded Districts')
1940s stalemate

Congress accepted linguistic provinces in principle; the Raj deferred ('after the war'); **the 1947-49 rethink — Dhar Commission (1948: language no basis) & JVP (1949: caution, but 'Andhra could be conceded minus Madras city')**
**The climax**

**Swami Sitaram's 1951 fast** (withdrawn on Vinoba's counsel) → **Potti Sriramulu's fast (19 Oct – 15 Dec 1952, Madras — 58 days, death)** → riots → Nehru conceded → **Andhra State, 1 October 1953** (11 districts; **Kurnool capital** per Sri Bagh's spirit; **T. Prakasam first CM; C.M. Trivedi Governor**) — **the first linguistic state**, forcing the SRC (1953) and the 1956 map

sections.heading: The leaders — and the movement's grammar

items: **The galaxy** (detailed portraits HCOA-065/066): **Konda Venkatappayya** ('Desabhakta'; the movement's parliamentary voice — his 1913-20s advocacy and the Andhra PCC), **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (ideologue-historian; linguistic-province theorist inside Congress), **T. Prakasam** ('Andhra Kesari'), **B.N. Sarma, Nyapathi Subba Rao ('Andhra Bhishma')** — the 1913 founders' bench, **Gadicherla & Ayyanki** (culture-infrastructure wing), **Swami Sitaram (Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri)** and **Potti Sriramulu** — the fasting saints; women — **Ponaka Kanakamma** and the Mahasabha's women's conferences (Andhra Mahila Sabha network).

**The movement's grammar**: petition (memorials to Montagu 1917-18) + institution-building (university, libraries, press) + Congress-internal lobbying (PCC, resolutions) + regional settlement (Sri Bagh — managing sub-regional equity BEFORE statehood: a lesson 2014 would re-teach) + finally satyagraha's ultimate instrument (the fast unto death) — constitutional method's full keyboard.

**Assessment**: the Andhra movement proved regional identity and Indian nationalism were **allies, not rivals** — its leaders were simultaneously Congress's all-India men (Pattabhi's presidency, Prakasam's premiership of composite Madras 1946-47); its success wrote the template (and the SRC) for India's federal map; its unfinished sub-regional equity file (Sri Bagh's fate) became AP's recurring inner question.

sections.heading: 🏺 Deep mastery — the Andhra Mahasabha & the province idea

items: **The province imagined:** the demand for a separate **Telugu-speaking province** grew from cultural pride and grievance at being a linguistic minority in the Madras Presidency; the **Andhra Mahasabha (first meeting 1913, Bapatla)** institutionalised it.

**Congress recognition:** Andhra was among the first **linguistic Provincial Congress Committees (1917)** — the Congress's early acceptance of the linguistic principle it would later implement nationally.

**Two Andhra Mahasabhas:** the coastal-Andhra cultural-political body, and the **Telangana Andhra Mahasabha** under the Nizam (which turned radical/communist, feeding the Telangana armed struggle) — distinguish them.
**Grammar of the movement:** language + culture + economic grievance (neglect within the Presidency) = the case for statehood.

prelimsPointers: **Andhra Mahasabha** — first session at **Bapatla, 1913**; demanded a separate Telugu province.
Congress conceded **linguistic Provincial Committees** in 1917 (Andhra among the first).
**First Andhra Mahasabha: Bapatla, 26-27 May 1913; president Bayya Narasimheswara Sarma**.
**Andhra PCC carved out 1917-18** — among India's first linguistic PCCs; Nagpur (1920) generalised the principle.
**'Rayalaseema'** coined by **Chilukuri Narayana Rao (1928)** for the Ceded Districts.
**Sri Bagh Pact (1937)** — signed at Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's Madras home ('Sri Bagh'): Circars-Rayalaseema settlement (university/HC/capital balance, irrigation priority).
**Dhar Commission (1948)** rejected, **JVP Committee (1949)** conditionally allowed Andhra (sans Madras city).
**Swami Sitaram's fast: 1951** (35+ days, withdrawn); **Potti Sriramulu: fasted 19 Oct–15 Dec 1952 at Bulusu Sambamurthy's Madras house; died day 58**.
**Andhra State: 1 October 1953 — 11 districts, Kurnool capital, T. Prakasam CM**; High Court at Guntur.
**Nyapathi Subba Rao Pantulu** — 'Andhra Bhishma', a founding father of the Mahasabha.
mainsAngles: From Bapatla to Kurnool — periodise the forty-year Andhra movement and its methods.
Regional identity proved nationalism's ally — argue with the Andhra movement's Congress-internal career.
The Sri Bagh Pact attempted equity before statehood — assess its provisions and afterlife.
Why did the Andhra demand succeed only through a martyr's fast despite decades of constitutional method?
The first linguistic state forced federal India's redesign — evaluate Andhra 1953 as the SRC's trigger.

glossary.definition: The annual conference-movement (from Bapatla 1913) demanding a Telugu province — the Andhra identity's political parliament.
Congress's language-based provincial committee — the Andhra PCC (1917-18) pioneering the principle Nagpur 1920 adopted.
The 1937 Circars-Rayalaseema gentlemen's settlement on capital, high court, university and irrigation priorities — sub-regional federalism's first Andhra draft.
The 1948 commission (language no basis) and 1949 Nehru-Patel-Pattabhi committee (cautious concession) — the founding-era brakes on linguistic states.
Satyagraha's terminal instrument — Sriramulu's 58-day fast converting a deferred demand into an irresistible one.
The 'greater Andhra' goal — uniting Andhra State with Telangana — realised as AP (1956) and revisited in 2014.

sections.heading: Six lives of the Andhra struggle

rows: **Alluri Sitarama Raju (1897-1924)**

Sanyasi-rebel of the Visakhapatnam agency; organised Koya-Bagata hill people against **forest-law podu bans, vetti and muttadar oppression**; the **Rampa/Manyam rebellion (Aug 1922-May 1924)** — guerrilla raids on **Chintapalli, Krishnadevipeta, Rajavommangi** police stations (arms seizures), jungle warfare humbling the Malabar Special Police; betrayed, **executed at Koyyuru (7 May 1924)**, tied to a tree and shot

'**Manyam Veerudu**' — the fusion figure: tribal grievance + nationalist consciousness (he invoked NCM's context while rejecting its pacifism); 125th-anniversary national commemorations (2022, Bhimavaram statue) renewed his memory
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya (1889-1928)**

Edinburgh-educated; 'Andhra Ratna'; led **Chirala-Perala (1921)** — evacuated ~13-15,000 townspeople to **Ramnagar** for 11 months against municipal imposition; Ramadandu volunteer corps; jailed; Kakinada Congress (1923)'s singing organiser
Constructive satyagraha's most audacious experiment — a town seceding from the Raj; oratory-music as mobilisation ('the singing leader')
**Konda Venkatappayya (1866-1948)**
'**Desabhakta**'; Krishna Patrika founder-editor phase; Andhra movement's father-figure (1913-); Andhra PCC's first helmsman; legislator; Gandhi's trusted Andhra lieutenant
The movement's respectability and persistence — petition-to-satyagraha bridge across four decades
**Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya (1880-1959)**

Machilipatnam doctor-turned-Congressman; **founder: Andhra Bank (1923), Andhra Insurance, Bhagyalakshmi Bank**; historian — ***History of the Indian National Congress* (1935/1946-47)**; lost to Bose (Tripuri 1939); **Congress President (Jaipur 1948)**; Ahmednagar prison chronicler; later **Governor of Madhya Pradesh (1952-57)**
Ideologue of linguistic provinces + swadeshi financier + the Congress's official memory — the institution-builder face of Andhra nationalism
**Ponaka Kanakamma (1892-1963)**

Nellore's Gandhian matriarch; salt-satyagraha organiser (Mypadu's backbone), khadi-Harijan work; **founded Kasturidevi Vidyalayam (Nellore girls' school)**; jailed (first Andhra women's cohort); Sriramulu's Nellore-era patron
Women's leadership normalised — funding, organising and jail-going in one person
**Dokka Seethamma (1841-1909)**

Godavari's legendary annadatri of **Lankala Gannavaram** — fed every traveller-pilgrim across caste lines for decades ('Apara Annapurna'); the Raj-era legend: her name invoked at the 1902 Delhi Durbar honours narrative
Service-as-dharma folk sainthood — the pre-political moral capital the movements later drew upon; **Godavari's aqueduct (2019) named for her** — living memory

items: **Spectrum logic**: armed tribal revolt (Alluri) — audacious civil disobedience (Duggirala) — constitutional persistence (Konda) — institutional nationalism (Pattabhi) — women's organising (Kanakamma) — pre-political seva (Seethamma): the Andhra struggle's full keyboard in six octaves; an answer that plays them as a SPECTRUM (not a list) earns the analysis mark.

**Alluri's deeper file** (the exam's favourite): causes — **Madras Forest Act 1882's** podu criminalisation, muttadar-contractor extraction (the Gudem road-works wage fraud), 1916-22 grievance build-up; methods — guerrilla + moral authority (warned stations before raids); state response — Malabar Special Police, **Rutherford's** scorched drive; legacy — agency protective regulations' reinforcement, the **1/70 (LTR 1959/70)** lineage of tribal land protection; historiography — 'primitive rebel' vs 'nationalist revolutionary': hold both.

**Chirala-Perala's arithmetic**: municipal upgradation = property-tax jump on a poor weaving town; Duggirala's answer — exodus, parallel town, eleven months of self-taxed order — failed materially (exhaustion, his arrest), succeeded morally (the Raj's legitimacy visibly optional); Gandhi's mixed verdict is the honest footnote.

sections.heading: 🏺 Deep mastery — the lives that carried the struggle

items: **The makers:** **Konda Venkatappayya** (architect of the Andhra movement), **Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (historian of the Congress, statehood advocate), **Tanguturi Prakasam** ('Andhra Kesari' — the lion who bared his chest to police guns, first CM of Andhra State), **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** (Chirala-Perala satyagraha), and **N.G. Ranga** (peasant leader).
**Reading the six together:** they fused **national freedom + linguistic statehood + social/peasant reform** — Andhra's struggle was simultaneously anti-colonial and identity-affirming.
**Prakasam's symbolism:** the 'Andhra Kesari' episode (baring his chest during a boycott) became the movement's iconic image of courage.
**Significance:** these lives embody how the all-India movement and the sub-national aspiration reinforced each other in Andhra.

sections.heading: The Granthalaya trio — Ayyanki, Gadicherla, Kasinathuni

rows: **Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya (1890-1979)**
Vijayawada's librarian-general of the nation; Congress worker; edited movement journals

**Founded the Andhradesa Grandhalaya Sangham (1914)** and steered its conferences; launched **Grandhalaya Sarvasvam (1916)**; moved the **All India Public Library Association (1919)** and its all-India conferences; pressed library legislation for decades (the 1960 AP Act his life's codicil) — **'Father of the Indian library movement'**; Rao Sahib title returned during NCM
**Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao (1883-1960)**

Vandemataram-era firebrand (expelled from Rajahmundry College's teachership context, 1907); **jailed for 'Viplavam' in *Swarajya* (1908-09)** — Andhra's first sedition-celebrity; Home Rule organiser; Andhra movement stalwart; scholar-translator

Ran libraries as national schools — the **Sarvottama/reading-room network of Rayalaseema-coastal towns**; librarianship-journalism-education fused; presided over library conferences; his life the proof that the reading room WAS the barricade
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao (1867-1938)**

'**Desoddharaka**' & 'Viswadata'; pharmacist-industrialist (**Amrutanjan, 1893**) turned press baron — **Andhra Patrika (1908 weekly Bombay → 1914 Madras daily)**, **Bharati (1924)**, **Andhra Grandhamala** book series; Congress financier; **host of the Sri Bagh Pact (1937 — his Madras residence)**

Bankrolled the print-library ecosystem: cheap classics via Grandhamala, the Patrika's library-movement advocacy, philanthropy to reading rooms and schools — the movement's treasury and megaphone in one

sections.heading: The trio as a system — and the movement's economics

items: **Division of labour**: Ayyanki = **organisation** (associations, journals, legislation-lobbying); Gadicherla = **cadre & content** (the librarian-educator model, nationalist prestige); Kasinathuni = **capital & circulation** (money, presses, cheap books) — a complete civil-society production system: organise-staff-finance.

**Economics of a village library**: local subscription + patron gift (often a widow's or merchant's donation — the Vetapalem model) + Grandhamala's cheap editions + travelling boxes; the ADLA's conferences standardised catalogues and training — indigenous institutional design a half-century before 'NGO capacity building'.

**Politics carried**: the trio's libraries hosted NCM-CDM organising; Gadicherla's sedition halo and Ayyanki's returned title bound the movement to nationalism's ledger; Kasinathuni's Patrika made 'library' a page-one cause. **Legacy**: AIPLA → Indian Library Association lineage; the 1948/1960 Acts; AP's ~4,000+ public-library network and the Granthalaya cess — their statute-shadow.
**One-line verdict**: they built the nation's **memory infrastructure** — before Andhra had a state, it had a catalogue.

sections.heading: 🏺 Deep mastery — the Granthalaya trio as a system

items: **The trio:** **Ayyanki Venkata Ramanaiah, Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, and Vavilala Gopalakrishnayya** — organisers who turned the **library movement** into a state-wide network of civic awakening.
**The library as system:** reading rooms + Telugu books + newspapers + public lectures created a decentralised infrastructure of literacy and nationalism — 'each library a cell of the movement'.
**Link to statehood:** the library and cultural movements built the literate, self-aware Telugu public that demanded and sustained the case for Andhra.
**Significance:** an instructive model of how cultural institution-building underpins political mobilisation — a strong, distinctive answer point.

prelimsPointers: **Ayyanki Venkata Ramanaiah** — organiser of the Andhra Granthalaya (library) movement.
The library movement functioned as the civic-cultural base of the Andhra statehood struggle.
**Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya** — ADLA (1914), **Grandhalaya Sarvasvam (1916)**, AIPLA (**1919**); hailed 'Father of the Indian library movement'.
**Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — prosecuted for the ***Swarajya* 'Viplavam' editorial (1908)**; Home Rule & Andhra movement leader; celebrated librarian-educator.

**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** — founded **Amrutanjan (1893)**; **Andhra Patrika** (weekly 1908, daily 1914), **Bharati (1924)**, **Andhra Grandhamala**; honorifics **'Desoddharaka'/'Viswadata'**; his home hosted the **Sri Bagh Pact (1937)**.
AIPLA's first conference lineage fed the **Indian Library Association (1933)**.
**AP Public Libraries Act 1960** (with the Madras 1948 Act) — the movement's legislative harvest; library cess funds the network.
**Vetapalem's Saraswata Niketanam (1918)** — the model village library-archive of the era.
